title: Eigenvector Varieties
authors: Sandra Di Rocco, Bernd Sturmfels, Svala Sverrisdóttir
abstract: Any linear space of square matrices has an associated eigenvector variety. Its points are eigenvectors of matrices from that linear space. We present a systematic study of eigenvector varieties, with focus on Lie algebras and Hamiltonians of quantum systems.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework to study eigenvector varieties associated with linear families of quantum Hamiltonians. By employing advanced tools from algebraic geometry, it determines the precise geometric structure (dimension and degree) of these varieties for various physical models, such as fermionic and bosonic systems.
main_problem: The paper systematically studies the geometry of 'eigenvector varieties,' $E(H)$, which are subvarieties in projective space whose points correspond to eigenvectors for matrices drawn from a linear space $H$ of quantum system Hamiltonians.
main_result: Key results characterize these varieties using tools from algebraic geometry, showing that for fermionic systems, the variety is related to Grassmannians, and for bosonic systems, it relates to Veronese or Chow varieties.
method: The analysis heavily employs advanced algebraic geometry techniques, including determinantal theory (minors of matrices), incidence varieties, elimination ideals, and intersection theory using Chow classes.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum mechanical systems modeled by Hamiltonians $H$ that are linear combinations of basis operators ($H = \sum t_i H_i$). Specific models include fermionic one-body operators (leading to Grassmannians) and bosonic one-body operators (leading to Veronese varieties).
key_observables: The dimension, degree, and irreducible components of the eigenvector variety $E(H)$ are key observables.
important_parameters: The dimensionality ($n$) of the Hilbert space, the number of parameters ($d$), and the structure of the underlying Lie algebra ($\mathfrak{g}$) govern the geometry.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes generic conditions on the basis matrices $H_i$ or that certain associated varieties are irreducible to derive clean dimension formulas.
figures_summary: No specific figure descriptions were extracted, but the notes reference tables providing numerical verification of dimensional conjectures for fermionic operators.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general algebraic characterizations (defining $E(H)$ via minors) to specialized physical applications. It systematically analyzes cases like generic pencils ($d=2$), 3D spaces ($d=3$), and finally tackles specific quantum models: fermionic one-body operators ($	ext{Gr}(k, m)$), bosonic one-body operators (Veronese varieties), and general Lie algebra representations.
why_interesting: This work provides deep geometric insights into the spectral properties of Hamiltonians. Understanding $E(H)$ helps characterize the set of possible ground states or low-energy excitations in complex quantum systems, linking spectral theory directly to algebraic geometry.
